classification: useful algorithm; useful benchmark (algorithm + dataset pair); outdated-but-prior-art
notes: GitHub API: archived=true (read-only), last push 2024-05-11, 14 commits total. Real-data level 3: Twist-synthesised 10,000 x 110-nt strands, PCR, ONT MinION (LQK-LSK109), 269,709 reads. The paper's coded-vs-uncoded results use MR-code/conv-code decoders on this dataset; the 10,000 strands are random (not MR-encoded), so how 'coded' real-data experiments were formed is not clear from the text I read (unverified). Limitations stated in paper: soft outputs of Trellis BMA are not ideally calibrated; multi-trace exact trellis exponential in #traces; BMALA-HD beats Trellis BMA in achievable rate for >6 traces; outer code and sequence-number overhead not implemented/neglected. License MIT: compatible for a benchmark harness (must keep MIT notice). Dataset caveat: authors' own 'Note added 8/12/2024' says the 10,000 centers are NOT uniformly random (generation bug) and some clusters may be malformed.

purpose: Rank/unrank codec: map binary strings of length n to quaternary strings of length N with max homopolymer run <= k (k=1..5), achieving the information-theoretic rate for the constraint (as n->infinity) via an FSM path-counting enumerative code with GMP big integers.

encoding.mapping: enumerative (lexicographic N-th path in a run-length FSM); k=1 reduces to base-2->base-3 conversion (6 bits -> 4 bases, rate 1.5 in the slides; finite-length rate 1.5818 at N=110 per my run); digits {0..3} map to ACGT by caller

ecc.other: none (pure constrained mapping, no error correction; a single indel/sub propagates across the big-integer decode)

storage_architecture.format: two C++ classes in one .cpp (BoundedHomopolymerEncoder/Decoder) + BHE_rates.cpp
storage_architecture.api: C++ header-style include; CLI driver (round-trip on random bits)

performance.throughputs: README: ~50 Mbps encode, ~80 Mbps decode, single core. My re-run on this host (8-core box, g++ -O3, k=3, N=150 bases, 297 bits max, 2000 random trials, single thread): encode 14 ms total, decode 8 ms total for 2000 strands => ~42 Mbit/s encode, ~74 Mbit/s decode, i.e. consistent with README. Measured by me 2026-10-05; not independently validated.
performance.parallelism: none built in ('easily parallelized across cores' per README)

testing.unit: no test suite; CLI does randomised round-trip and prints ERROR on mismatch
testing.reproducibility: builds with one g++ line + libgmp; I built it successfully

classification: useful algorithm (constrained coding primitive); complementary research
notes: Verified rates: bhe_rates 96 => k=1..5: 1.583/1.917/1.979/1.990/1.990 b/base (README); I reproduced bhe_rates 110 => 1.5818/1.9182/1.9818/1.9909/1.9909. Slide table gives asymptotic limits 1.5850/1.9227/1.9823/1.9957/1.9989 (k=1..5). Repo is new (created 2025-09-24, 8 commits, not archived). MIT licence => OK to run in a benchmark harness (separate process). Limitations: homopolymer constraint only (no GC, no motifs); no error-correction, so must be paired with an inner/outer ECC; big-integer arithmetic scales super-linearly with N; max k=5.
